### Background

Follow-up to deepspeedai/DeepSpeed#8732 and its
[review suggestions](https://github.com/deepspeedai/DeepSpeed/pull/8732#pullrequestreview-5542240098).
Training updates invalidate the continuous rollout graph, so steady-state latency alone does not capture the cost of alternating training and generation.

### Implementation status

The initial benchmark records CUDA-synchronized latency and throughput for eager / graph rollouts around one real SGD update. Each measured call's tokens, attention masks, and response offsets are checked against native Hugging Face `generate()` using the same weights.

### Existing GPU measurements

Recorded on an RTX A4500 (20 GiB), PyTorch 2.9.1+cu128 / CUDA 12.8, Transformers 5.20.1, FP16, using a randomly initialized tiny Llama. Steady-state values are medians of 10 calls; first-call values are single samples.

| Phase | Eager (ms) | CUDA Graph (ms) |
| --- | ---: | ---: |
| First call | 240.182 | 61.933 |
| Steady state | 228.014 | 45.424 |
| First call after SGD update | 226.304 | 58.800 |
| Steady state after update | 234.919 | 45.281 |

Graph first-call overhead was 16.509 ms before SGD and 13.519 ms afterward; the training update took 55.849 ms. These are synthetic observations, not production-model performance claims. **The overhead values are end-to-end differences, not isolated capture timings.**

Reproduce on the benchmark checkout with the Issue 4 fix:

```bash
python -m benchmarks.rollout.bench_cuda_graph_first_call \
    --requests 8 --batch-size 4 --prompt-len 32 --max-new-tokens 32 \
    --iterations 10 --output rollout-first-call.json
```

CUDA / model libraries were initialized without warming up the rollout graph; each phase measured eager before graph. The original combined working tree reported **60 passed, 1 skipped** and passing pre-commit checks. The skip required an optional pretrained model. This benchmark was not rerun during the separate Issue 4 validation.

### Remaining work and acceptance criteria

- Separate cache / static-buffer allocation, warmup, and capture timings from total rollout latency, without double-counting.
- Report per-phase capture counts, allocated / reserved and peak GPU memory, latency, and generated-token throughput.
- Measure repeated training / rollout cycles with real optimizer updates; preserve the four phases and generation-parity checks.
- Keep synchronized timing, fixed inputs, reproducible commands, and complete model / attention / hardware / software / workload metadata. Clearly label synthetic versus pretrained-model results; none of the latter are available yet.

### Scope and dependencies

Depends on deepspeedai/DeepSpeed#8732 and, on Transformers 5.20.1, Issue 4. Keep the runtime fix separate. Measure existing behavior without weakening parameter-version checks. Benchmark code and usage belong in `benchmarks/rollout/bench_cuda_graph_first_call.py` and `benchmarks/README.md`, not the Issue 4 branch.

CC @delock

@@ -4,3 +4,64 @@ If you are looking for DeepSpeed benchmarks, please see the following resources:
 
 1. [Communication Benchmarking Suite](https://github.com/deepspeedai/DeepSpeedExamples/tree/master/benchmarks/communication)
 2. [Inference Benchmarks](https://github.com/deepspeedai/DeepSpeedExamples/tree/master/benchmarks/inference)
+
+## Continuous rollout CUDA Graph first-call costs
+
+Run from the repository root on one CUDA GPU with PyTorch, Transformers, and
+DeepSpeed installed:
+
+Use Transformers 4.57.6 with the current runtime. Transformers 5.x requires the
+query-offset compatibility fix in [deepspeedai/DeepSpeed#8852](https://github.com/deepspeedai/DeepSpeed/pull/8852),
+which is intentionally kept separate from this benchmark.
+
+```bash
+python -m benchmarks.rollout.bench_cuda_graph_first_call \
+    --requests 8 --batch-size 4 --prompt-len 32 --max-new-tokens 32 \
+    --iterations 10 --output rollout-first-call.json
+```
+
+This offline benchmark uses a randomly initialized two-layer Llama, native
+Transformers attention, greedy decoding, and more requests than physical slots
+to exercise continuous refills. EOS is disabled for a fixed token workload.
+It compares eager and CUDA Graph rollouts sharing the same model before and
+after a real next-token-loss backward pass and in-place SGD update.
+
+The JSON report includes synchronized wall-clock latency samples, median/min/max,
+generated-token throughput, model/workload configuration, library versions, and
+GPU name/memory. Each mode reports `first_call`, `steady_state`,
+`first_call_after_update`, and `steady_state_after_update`. The training update
+is timed separately; output tokens, masks, and response offsets must match an
+independent native Hugging Face `generate()` reference for every measured call,
+both before and after the update.
+
+There is **no rollout warmup before either first-call measurement**. A non-cached
+model forward and native reference generation initialize CUDA/model libraries
+before measurement; eager is measured before graph in each phase. First graph
+calls include cache allocation, capture warmup, graph capture, and generation.
+Post-update calls include any
+invalidation/recapture required by the rollout implementation. Stable calls reuse
+the same rollout, shapes, and weights. Internal profiling is disabled to avoid
+per-stage synchronization overhead.
+
+`graph_first_call_premium_ms` and `graph_post_update_premium_ms` subtract the
+corresponding graph steady-state median from the first-call latency. These are
+observed end-to-end premiums, **not isolated capture timings**; they can be
+negative under measurement noise. First calls are single samples, not medians
+across independent captures. Repeat the command in fresh processes for
+first-call distributions. This small synthetic model measures rollout overhead,
+not pretrained-model quality or production-model speedup.
+
+Example measured with the command above on an NVIDIA RTX A4500 (20 GiB),
+PyTorch 2.9.1+cu128 / CUDA 12.8, Transformers 5.20.1 with the query-offset fix, FP16:
+
+| Phase | Eager latency (ms) | CUDA Graph latency (ms) |
+|---|---:|---:|
+| First call | 240.182 | 61.933 |
+| Steady state (10-call median) | 228.014 | 45.424 |
+| First call after SGD update | 226.304 | 58.800 |
+| Post-update steady state (10-call median) | 234.919 | 45.281 |
+
+The observed graph first-call premium was 16.509 ms; the post-update premium was
+13.519 ms. The separately timed training update took 55.849 ms. All measured
+outputs matched native generation before and after the update. These are one
+run's illustrative results, not performance thresholds.

@@ -0,0 +1,204 @@
+# SPDX-License-Identifier: Apache-2.0
+# DeepSpeed Team
+"""Measure continuous rollout latency before and after a training update."""
+
+import argparse
+import json
+import statistics
+import time
+from pathlib import Path
+from types import SimpleNamespace
+
+import torch
+import transformers
+from transformers import LlamaConfig, LlamaForCausalLM
+
+from deepspeed.accelerator import get_accelerator
+from deepspeed.runtime.rollout.base import RolloutRequest, SamplingConfig
+from deepspeed.runtime.rollout.hybrid_engine_rollout import HybridEngineRollout, HybridEngineRolloutConfig
+
+
+def positive_int(value):
+    value = int(value)
+    if value < 1:
+        raise argparse.ArgumentTypeError("must be positive")
+    return value
+
+
+def parse_args(argv=None):
+    parser = argparse.ArgumentParser(description=__doc__)
+    parser.add_argument("--requests", type=positive_int, default=8)
+    parser.add_argument("--batch-size", type=positive_int, default=4)
+    parser.add_argument("--prompt-len", type=positive_int, default=32)
+    parser.add_argument("--max-new-tokens", type=positive_int, default=32)
+    parser.add_argument("--iterations", type=positive_int, default=10)
+    parser.add_argument("--dtype", choices=("float32", "float16", "bfloat16"), default="float16")
+    parser.add_argument("--seed", type=int, default=1234)
+    parser.add_argument("--output", type=Path, help="Also write the JSON report to this file")
+    args = parser.parse_args(argv)
+    if args.max_new_tokens < 2:
+        parser.error("--max-new-tokens must be at least 2 to exercise graph replay")
+    if args.prompt_len < 2:
+        parser.error("--prompt-len must be at least 2 for the next-token training loss")
+    if args.requests <= args.batch_size:
+        parser.error("--requests must exceed --batch-size to exercise continuous slot refills")
+    return args
+
+
+def measure_calls(rollout, request, sampling, iterations, expected):
+    accelerator = get_accelerator()
+    latencies = []
+    generated_tokens = 0
+    for _ in range(iterations):
+        accelerator.synchronize()
+        start = time.perf_counter()
+        output = rollout.generate(request, sampling)
+        accelerator.synchronize()
+        latencies.append((time.perf_counter() - start) * 1000.0)
+
+        # Keep correctness checks and device-to-host copies outside the timed interval.
+        actual = (output.input_ids.cpu(), output.attention_mask.cpu(), output.response_start_idx.cpu())
+        for observed, reference in zip(actual, expected):
+            torch.testing.assert_close(observed, reference, rtol=0, atol=0)
+        response_mask = torch.arange(output.seq_len)[None, :] >= actual[2][:, None]
+        generated_tokens += int((actual[1] * response_mask).sum())
+
+    return {
+        "latencies_ms": latencies,
+        "median_ms": statistics.median(latencies),
+        "min_ms": min(latencies),
+        "max_ms": max(latencies),
+        "generated_tokens": generated_tokens,
+        "tokens_per_second": generated_tokens / (sum(latencies) / 1000.0),
+    }
+
+
+def training_step(model, request):
+    accelerator = get_accelerator()
+    optimizer = torch.optim.SGD(model.parameters(), lr=0.01)
+    model.train()
+    accelerator.synchronize()
+    start = time.perf_counter()
+    loss = model(input_ids=request.prompt_ids,
+                 attention_mask=request.prompt_attention_mask,
+                 labels=request.prompt_ids,
+                 use_cache=False).loss
+    loss.backward()
+    optimizer.step()
+    optimizer.zero_grad(set_to_none=True)
+    accelerator.synchronize()
+    elapsed_ms = (time.perf_counter() - start) * 1000.0
+    if not torch.isfinite(loss):
+        raise RuntimeError("The training update produced a non-finite loss")
+    model.eval()
+    return {"latency_ms": elapsed_ms, "loss": loss.item(), "optimizer": "SGD", "learning_rate": 0.01}
+
+
+@torch.no_grad()
+def reference_output(model, request, sampling):
+    output_ids = model.generate(
+        input_ids=request.prompt_ids,
+        attention_mask=request.prompt_attention_mask,
+        max_new_tokens=sampling.max_new_tokens,
+        do_sample=False,
+        eos_token_id=None,
+        pad_token_id=0,
+    )
+    return (output_ids.cpu(), torch.ones_like(output_ids, device="cpu"),
+            torch.full((output_ids.shape[0], ), request.prompt_ids.shape[1], dtype=torch.long))
+
+
+def run_benchmark(args):
+    accelerator = get_accelerator()
+    if accelerator.device_name() != "cuda" or not accelerator.is_available():
+        raise RuntimeError("This benchmark requires a CUDA GPU")
+    accelerator.set_device(0)
+    torch.manual_seed(args.seed)
+    device = torch.device(accelerator.current_device_name())
+    config = LlamaConfig(
+        vocab_size=256,
+        hidden_size=128,
+        intermediate_size=256,
+        num_hidden_layers=2,
+        num_attention_heads=4,
+        num_key_value_heads=2,
+        max_position_embeddings=(args.prompt_len + args.max_new_tokens) * args.requests,
+        pad_token_id=0,
+        eos_token_id=None,
+        attention_dropout=0.0,
+        tie_word_embeddings=False,
+    )
+    config._attn_implementation = "eager"
+    model = LlamaForCausalLM(config).to(device=device, dtype=getattr(torch, args.dtype)).eval()
+    prompt_ids = torch.randint(1, config.vocab_size, (args.requests, args.prompt_len), device=device)
+    request = RolloutRequest(prompt_ids, torch.ones_like(prompt_ids))
+    sampling = SamplingConfig(max_new_tokens=args.max_new_tokens, temperature=0, continuous_batch_size=args.batch_size)
+    tokenizer = SimpleNamespace(pad_token_id=0, eos_token_id=None)
+    engine = SimpleNamespace(module=model)
+    rollouts = {
+        mode: HybridEngineRollout(engine, tokenizer, HybridEngineRolloutConfig(use_graph_capture=(mode == "graph")))
+        for mode in ("eager", "graph")
+    }
+    results = {mode: {} for mode in rollouts}
+
+    # Warm CUDA/model libraries without touching either rollout's graph state.
+    with torch.no_grad():
+        model(input_ids=prompt_ids, attention_mask=request.prompt_attention_mask, use_cache=False)
+    accelerator.synchronize()
+
+    update = None
+    for first_phase, steady_phase in (("first_call", "steady_state"), ("first_call_after_update",
+                                                                       "steady_state_after_update")):
+        if first_phase == "first_call_after_update":
+            update = training_step(model, request)
+        expected = reference_output(model, request, sampling)
+        for mode, rollout in rollouts.items():
+            results[mode][first_phase] = measure_calls(rollout, request, sampling, 1, expected)
+            results[mode][steady_phase] = measure_calls(rollout, request, sampling, args.iterations, expected)
+
+    graph = results["graph"]
+    return {
+        "environment": {
+            "gpu": torch.cuda.get_device_name(0),  #ignore-cuda: accelerator has no GPU model-name API
+            "total_memory_bytes": accelerator.total_memory(0),
+            "torch": torch.__version__,
+            "cuda": torch.version.cuda,
+            "transformers": transformers.__version__,
+        },
+        "workload": {
+            "model": "random tiny Llama (no download)",
+            "model_config": config.to_dict(),
+            "dtype": args.dtype,
+            "seed": args.seed,
+            "requests": args.requests,
+            "continuous_batch_size": args.batch_size,
+            "prompt_len": args.prompt_len,
+            "max_new_tokens": args.max_new_tokens,
+            "iterations": args.iterations,
+            "eos_disabled": True,
+            "profiling_enabled": False,
+        },
+        "results":
+        results,
+        "training_update":
+        update,
+        "graph_first_call_premium_ms":
+        graph["first_call"]["median_ms"] - graph["steady_state"]["median_ms"],
+        "graph_post_update_premium_ms":
+        graph["first_call_after_update"]["median_ms"] - graph["steady_state_after_update"]["median_ms"],
+        "outputs_match":
+        True,
+    }
+
+
+def main():
+    args = parse_args()
+    report = run_benchmark(args)
+    serialized = json.dumps(report, indent=2)
+    if args.output is not None:
+        args.output.write_text(serialized + "\n")
+    print(serialized)
+
+
+if __name__ == "__main__":
+    main()

+from unittest.mock import patch
 
 import pytest
 import torch
@@ -14,6 +15,33 @@
 from deepspeed.runtime.rollout.hybrid_engine_rollout import HybridEngineRollout, HybridEngineRolloutConfig
 
 
+def test_continuous_graph_first_call_benchmark_on_cuda():
+    accelerator = get_accelerator()
+    if not accelerator.is_available() or accelerator.device_name() != "cuda":
+        pytest.skip("CUDA is required for CUDA graph benchmark coverage")
+
+    from benchmarks.rollout.bench_cuda_graph_first_call import parse_args, run_benchmark
+
+    args = parse_args([
+        "--requests", "3", "--batch-size", "2", "--prompt-len", "4", "--max-new-tokens", "3", "--iterations", "2",
+        "--dtype", "float32"
+    ])
+    # Unchanged shapes must reuse captures until the optimizer updates weights.
+    with patch.object(accelerator, "capture_to_graph", wraps=accelerator.capture_to_graph) as capture:

+        assert capture.call_count == 2
+

+            assert measurement["generated_tokens"] == 3 * 3 * iterations

+            assert measurement["tokens_per_second"] > 0
+
